findings.finding: The fallback is 750 ms after the awaited tick, not a 750 ms bound on dispatch latency.
findings.detail: Reservation release wakes selection; a slow awaited tick prevents the wait from even beginning.

findings.finding: Selection offers 12 rows, not 12 starts. The vector lane has two slots; intake-large is singleton.
detail: One tick can start at most the lane's remaining slots, further bounded by memory and scratch.
intake-large, streaming-vector and streamed-profile share vector's two slots; their own runners are single.
Memory defaults to half host RAM; intake-large reserves 426 MiB, raw 415 MiB, profile 512 MiB.
An older memory/scratch refusal eventually prevents newer non-probe starts; existing exceptions stay.
The singleton allows one intake-large start per tick, but contains no 19-second timer.

findings.finding: The remaining explicit cross-lane barrier was awaited surface admission before worker starts.
detail: admitIntakeSurfaceParts reads all eligible surfaces, then awaits each selected item's transaction serially.
Those transactions can wait on case/source SHARE locks and reader admission advisory locks.
A slow pass delays every selected lane even when its selected jobs take only milliseconds.
Now one tracked pass runs independently; subsequent ticks cannot overlap it. Reader caps are unchanged.
Pass completion does not unconditionally wake dispatch: an empty pass must not cause a busy loop.
qualification: REH16 has no tick, SQL, lock or surface-pass timing. The exact 19-second runtime source is not proven.
The blocking path is reproduced offline with an 18.25-second surface perturbation matching the cadence.
Scratch remains awaited. Twelve actual offline probes of E:/ulpin-tmp were fast, not a runtime measurement.
No receipt supports blaming the 180-second lease or increasing any concurrency cap.

findings.finding: Pending order was probes, per-source lane row_number, then job created_at; no item continuity.
detail: Each state change creates a fresh conductor job; six earlier child jobs can precede the member's refresh.
Children have distinct source IDs, so per-source fairness does not group their common batch.
Only layout/profile preparation is regrouped at that batch's earliest existing G22 selection position.
Within it: stored wave, needs_answer/approved layout, original item creation, then job FIFO and ID tie-break.
The profile and subsequent answer retain the item's age rather than restarting at each job's creation.
Bulk point/raster/document parts keep G22 fairness; >12 sibling and 211-part controls pass offline.
There is no persisted opened-item focus in this task: stored layout state and officer wave are reused.
The batch's display sorts wave/name; scheduling uses FIFO within a wave rather than alphabetical names.

method: The real ZIP is probed and its GeoJSON extracted with existing readers, including size/CRC checks.
Six layer names are verified against the permitted watch receipt. No geometry or source content is saved.
Start at a fan-out-complete ready checkpoint: child job FIFO precedes an older member item's follow-up.
Stub spans come from QW1 bAlone: start 140 ms, raw 6170 ms, profile 6830 ms, question refresh 13 ms.
Layer stubs use those same measured member spans; separate layer service times are not available.
Surface delay 18250 ms is a cadence perturbation, not a measured REH16 surface-service duration.
Execute the real tick's SQL windows in memory, translating PostgreSQL array joins/casts for SQLite.
A fixed 8192 MiB disk answer isolates scheduling; this mix reserves zero scratch.
Memory is 1536 MiB; real singleton guards, lane admission, resource holds and release wakes execute.
whySmallest: Remove the cross-lane awaited barrier rather than raising lane or singleton caps.
Reuse stored item/layout/wave state in the existing selection, before LIMIT, rather than add a queue.
The replay eliminates repeated scheduling waits and demonstrates no sibling starvation.
It does not model mapping/draft execution, ZIP retention, browser observation or PostgreSQL performance.
